name: Christopher Kelk Ingold
summary: Dominant figure in physical organic chemistry who developed the concept of mesomerism and electronic theory of organic reactions.

name: Edith Hilda Ingold
summary: Chemist and co-author with Christopher Ingold.

name: Robert Robinson
summary: British chemist and pioneer of electronic theory, rival and colleague of Ingold.

name: G. N. Lewis
summary: American chemist who discovered the material constitution of the covalent bond.

name: Irving Langmuir
summary: Chemist who elaborated upon Lewis's foundation and introduced the octet and covalent bond concept.

name: Thomas Martin Lowry
summary: British chemist who introduced the concept of the double bond as containing both covalent and ionic attributes.

name: Arthur Lapworth
summary: British chemist who made major strides in the use of the Lewis-Langmuir theory.

name: Linus Pauling
summary: Chemist who developed resonance theory using quantum mechanics at the same time as Ingold.

name: Peter Debye
summary: Physicist who developed the dipole moment measurement technique used by Ingold.

name: Neville Sidgwick
summary: Ingold's fellow countryman who understood the application of quantum mechanics to chemistry.

name: J. F. Thorpe
summary: Ingold's mentor who headed the department at Imperial College.

name: Fritz Arndt
summary: Chemist who anticipated Ingold's concept of mesomerism through analysis of pyrones.

name: K. Hogendahl
summary: Researcher who completed the first dipole moment test for the NH2 group.

name: F. R. Shaw
summary: Collaborator with Ingold on partial rate factors for aromatic substitution.

name: C. C. N. Vass
summary: Collaborator with Ingold on the inductive effect in aromatic substitution.

name: George W. Wheland
summary: Coworker of Linus Pauling who introduced resonance theory.

name: J. Sherman
summary: Coworker of Linus Pauling who introduced resonance theory.

name: Charles W. Shoppee
summary: Author of the obituary notice for Sir Christopher Kelk Ingold.

name: Martin D. Saltzman
summary: Author of the source document, Professor of Natural Science at Providence College.

name: Leeds University
summary: University where Ingold was appointed Professor of Organic Chemistry.

name: Imperial College
summary: College where Ingold was a lecturer in the department headed by J. F. Thorpe.

name: Stanford University
summary: University where Ingold was on leave in 1932.

name: University of California, Berkeley
summary: University where G. N. Lewis worked and Ingold planned to visit.

name: Royal Society
summary: Scientific society of which Ingold was made a Fellow.

name: Faraday Society
summary: Society that sponsored a symposium at Cambridge in 1923.

name: British Association
summary: Organization where Langmuir lectured in Edinburgh in 1921.

name: Providence College
summary: College where Martin D. Saltzman is Professor of Natural Science.

name: Principles of an Electron Theory of Organic Reactions
summary: Chemical Reviews paper published by Ingold in 1934.

name: The Atom and the Molecule
summary: Pioneering paper by G. N. Lewis appearing in 1916.

name: The Nature of the Alternating Effect in Carbon Chains, Part V
summary: 1926 paper published by Ingold with his wife as co-author.

name: Significance of Tautomerism and of the Reactions of Aromatic Compounds in the Electronic Theory of Organic Reactions
summary: 1933 paper where Ingold introduced the term mesomerism.

name: Mesomerism and Tautomerism
summary: 1934 Nature paper by Ingold.

name: Structure and Mechanism in Organic Chemistry
summary: Book by Ingold, 2nd edition published in 1953.
